thought.text: The serve reported "cms ready" but on a drifted port. Let me check the actual state:

reasoning_content:
The serve log says "cms ready (1m11s)" — but that's a stale log? Wait, no: /tmp/zz-cms.log is the log of my new serve. It says "✓ cms ready (1m11s)". But port 39002 shows nothing, and the cms build process (2120MB) is still running...

Hmm, wait. Actually, that serve might have reported "ready" because... no, that's wrong. Looking again: the log says "✓ cms ready (1m11s)" and then displays the URL table — which means the serve considered cms to be ready. But my curl to 39002 fails, and the build process (2120MB) is still active.

Oh wait — I've figured out what happened. The serve's "ready" check probes the allocated port. When I ran `just serve --apps=cms`, ports.json was... let me think. At the start of zz-cms, ports.json was {app:39001, cms:39002, boards:39003}, with boards running on 39003 and 39001/39002 free. resolveDevServerPorts: for app (39001, free) → keep 39001; for cms (39002, free) → keep 39002; for boards (39003, in use) → reallocate a new port (34903!). Then it rewrites ports.json: {app:39001, cms:39002, boards:34903}.

Wait, but if that's the case then cms should be on 39002... The serve is saying "cms ready" — but maybe it's ready on a different port? Let me check the current contents of ports.json. The cms build process (174340, 2120MB) is still running — maybe it's actually a new build on 39002 that's still finishing its initial request handling (the first build on request)? Actually "cms ready (1m11s)" was displayed 1 minute 11 seconds after startup — that was early in my monitoring. And my curl to 39002 was failing at 000...

Hmm, wait, actually there might be 2 cms builds: an old one (banner on 34903) + the new one. The 2120MB process might be a new cms build that's still compiling (the "ready" line in the log is confusing).

Wait, let me re-read: `✓ cms ready (1m11s)` — then it outputs the URL table. That's the normal success path. Then serve keeps running (holding the dev server). So according to the serve, cms is serving on the port that was allocated. Which port? If resolveDevServerPorts kept 39002 for cms, then it should be serving on 39002. But curl 39002 = 000 (connection refused).

Could it be that... "ready" was determined on a different port because ports.json was modified by my earlier render? I should check ports.json right now, and also check which port the new build is actually listening on.

Actually, there's a simpler explanation: my kill (`xargs kill` against run-executor/nx.js) killed the process of the old cms build, but the old serve (161930) — I killed its group 161929 — hmm.

Wait, actually, looking at the tail of the log: the last line of the CMS log is a banner on 34903 — that's an old banner (from the zz-cms serve? or from before?). The zz-cms serve started around 22:47. If the cms build on 34903 is from the zz-cms serve... that would mean resolveDevServerPorts gave cms 34903 — that happens if 39002 was in use at that point (maybe an old process was still holding it). And then "cms ready" — but on 34903, not 39002! And nginx.conf is pointing to 39002 → 502!

And the 2120MB process might still be that cms build. But then why is curl 39002 refused — consistent: cms is on 34903.

So: at the start of zz-cms, 39002 must have been in use (leftover). And the cms banner (34903) in cms.log is from zz-cms. The reason my earlier `ss -ltnp` grep didn't show 34903 is... ss failed (the exit 1 might be from ss not existing, or from grep). Let me directly check ports.json and curl 34903.

action.command: cat /workspace/.urbo/workspace/ports.json; for p in 39002 34903; do curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "$p: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:$p/ 2>/dev/null || echo "$p: closed"; done; ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E "3900[0-9]|34903" || netstat -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E "3900[0-9]|34903"

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cat /workspace/.urbo/workspace/ports.json; for p in 39002 34903; do curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w \"$p: %{http_code}\\n\" http://127.0.0.1:$p/ 2>/dev/null || echo \"$p: closed\"; done; ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E \"3900[0-9]|34903\" || netstat -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E \"3900[0-9]|34903\"", "summary": "Check actual cms port and ports.json"}

summary: Check actual cms port and ports.json
